claims.text: Moderate-temperature aging of the rapidly solidified alloy nucleates and grows nanoscale Al–Mg-rich intermetallic precipitates.
Precipitation depletes the surrounding matrix in Mg.
Precipitation enriches the surrounding matrix in Al.
The resulting matrix partitioning promotes formation of a more continuous Al2O3 film during high-temperature oxidation.
Formation of the more continuous Al2O3 film lowers the oxidation rate.
Discrete Al–Mg-rich intermetallic precipitates act as cathodic sites relative to the matrix in aqueous chloride environments.
Cathodic intermetallic sites increase matrix anodic dissolution and accelerate localized chloride corrosion.
The as-quenched starting material is a non-equilibrium supersaturated solid solution with randomly distributed Mg and no or minimal discrete intermetallic phases.
The aging precipitates may be Al3Mg2 or similar Laves-type phases.
After aging, oxidation mass gain at 500 °C for 100 hours will decrease by approximately 20% relative to the as-quenched baseline.
After aging, corrosion current density in 3.5 wt% NaCl will increase by approximately a factor of two.
After aging, localized corrosion will become more pronounced.
The as-quenched alloy has an oxidation mass gain of approximately 60 mg/cm2 under the stated oxidation exposure.
The as-quenched alloy has a corrosion current density of approximately 5 µA/cm2 in 3.5 wt% NaCl.
The as-quenched alloy undergoes mostly uniform corrosion.
The proposed mechanism is valid for Al-rich alloys below 6 g/cm3 aged between 450 and 550 °C for 10 to 200 hours.
The proposed mechanism does not apply when aging produces a continuous brittle intermetallic network above 30% volume fraction.
The magnitudes of the oxidation and corrosion changes depend on precipitate volume fraction and spatial distribution.
Gd and Zn microalloying additions may modify the precipitate chemistry.

contradictions.description: The intervention specifies inert-atmosphere aging for corrosion specimens, whereas the falsification experiment says the aged comparison set is treated in air before corrosion testing. This changes both the prescribed intervention and the surface oxidation state, confounding the corrosion comparison.
The mediator identifies Al3Mg2 alongside 'similar Laves-type phases,' although Al3Mg2 is not itself a Laves phase; the proposed precipitate class is therefore crystallographically ambiguous.
